Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. 293	- 315 is a dependency for SFCC-270, 274, 316, 318, 404 — and **SFCC-316 (Zimmermann Benefits –
294	  Contentful) is Sprint 5, Ready for Development, assigned to Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz.** Someone else's
295	  active-sprint card is waiting on this. **Ship 315 first and standalone.**

298	
299	ACs: per line item — image; name to the right of the image; price; selected colour; selected size;
300	quantity with `+`/`–` either side; multiple items each individually identifiable; Remove and Wishlist
301	as **underlined text links below the stepper**; on mobile nothing truncated or hidden.
302	
303	**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): override base `product-item`.** Cart keeps using it. Separately,
304	upcoming wishlist work moves the account wishlist page onto `ZimmProductCard` (which already has a
305	`variation: 'wishlist'` with `showRemove`), so it stops consuming `product-item` at that point.
306	
307	Accurate consumer map — **two chains only**:
308	```
309	pages/cart  ->  components/product-item-list  ->  components/product-item
310	pages/account/wishlist  ->  components/product-item          (direct)
311	```
312	Checkout does **not** use it. The base has two separate line-item systems: `product-item` (the full
313	interactive row) and `item-variant/*` (a read-only composition used by `order-summary`, i.e. the
314	checkout summaries).
315	
316	**Copy-first scope — 3 files** from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/`:
317	`index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB),
318	each to `.tsx`. Base's own `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` are not copied — write our own.
319	
320	**The finding that changes the size of the job:** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content
321	through **five more base components** — `components/item-variant` plus `item-variant/item-image`,
322	`item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price`. So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's
323	*structure and controls*; the *content pieces* still come from `item-variant/*`. Styling those to
324	Figma means either overriding `item-variant/*` too — which also changes `order-summary`, and
325	therefore the checkout summaries — or not using them inside our override and composing the content
326	ourselves. **Decide this before starting: it is the difference between a 3-file override and an
327	8-file one with checkout blast radius.**
328	
329	**`shared/ui` barrel trap applies.** `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`.
330	Per the known trap, overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — 208 base files
331	import the barrel, so only overriding the barrel itself has any effect.
332	
333	**Bridge-pattern requirement:** because `product-item` is used internally by base components, the
334	override's **default export must stay API-compatible** (full original prop surface) so
335	`product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working. Per `overrideStyling.md`, put brand styling
336	in a **theme recipe**, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second
337	export that `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

95	Note it **sums across line items** — i.e. the existing code already assumes one SKU can occupy more
96	than one line.
97	
98	### 2.3 Basket merge: mode, default, and the same-product match rules
99	
100	`mergeBasket` request parameter `productItemMergeMode`:
101	`"higher_quantity" | "sum_quantities" | "saved_quantity" | "separate_item"`.
102	SDK doc: *"By default, the higher of the two basket quantities is used for each product."*
103	
104	Same-product match requires **all** of these to be equal:
105	> shipment · productId · option values · wishlist reference · inventory list id ·
106	> gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments
107	
108	> *"If any of the listed values don't match, then the item in the previous shopper's basket is
109	> copied to a **new line item** in the current shopper's basket."*
110	
111	Consequence: `higher_quantity` protects only the single-line case. Two lines of the same SKU that
112	differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag do **not** merge, and their quantities coexist —
113	so a SKU total can exceed the cap without any single line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic
114	differentiators are **Collect in Boutique** (separate shipment) and **boutique vs warehouse
115	inventory lists** (CAI-022). At plain cart with no fulfilment choice made, both baskets sit in the
116	same default shipment and inventory list, so they DO match and 2 + 2 → 2 under the default.
117	
118	### 2.4 Where merge is called, and with what
119	
120	Four base call sites, **all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`** (no merge mode):

Note it **sums across line items** — i.e. the existing code already assumes one SKU can occupy more
than one line.

### 2.3 Basket merge: mode, default, and the same-product match rules

`mergeBasket` request parameter `productItemMergeMode`:
`"higher_quantity" | "sum_quantities" | "saved_quantity" | "separate_item"`.
SDK doc: *"By default, the higher of the two basket quantities is used for each product."*

Same-product match requires **all** of these to be equal:
> shipment · productId · option values · wishlist reference · inventory list id ·
> gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments

> *"If any of the listed values don't match, then the item in the previous shopper's basket is
> copied to a **new line item** in the current shopper's basket."*

Consequence: `higher_quantity` protects only the single-line case. Two lines of the same SKU that
differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag do **not** merge, and their quantities coexist —
so a SKU total can exceed the cap without any single line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic
differentiators are **Collect in Boutique** (separate shipment) and **boutique vs warehouse
inventory lists** (CAI-022). At plain cart with no fulfilment choice made, both baskets sit in the
same default shipment and inventory list, so they DO match and 2 + 2 → 2 under the default.

### 2.4 Where merge is called, and with what

Four base call sites, **all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`** (no merge mode):
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js`
- `.../app/pages/login/index.jsx`
- `.../app/pages/social-login-redirect/index.jsx`
- `.../app/pages/checkout/partials/contact-info.jsx`

13	 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
14	 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
15	 *
16	 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
17	 * component from a new component":
18	 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
19	 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
20	 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
21	 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
22	 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
23	 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
24	 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
25	 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
26	 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
27	 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
28	 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
29	 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
30	 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
31	 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
32	 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
33	 *
34	 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
35	 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
36	 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
39	 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
40	 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
43	 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
44	 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
45	 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
46	 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
47	 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
48	 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
49	 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
50	 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
51	 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
52	 * tested requirement.
53	 *
54	 * Gift-card conditional stepper/actions suppression is NOT implemented at this step — see this
55	 * build's report for why (no real signal for a digital gift card line item was found anywhere in
56	 * this codebase or the commerce SDK types at time of writing; `GiftCertificateItem` exists in
57	 * the SDK but is a structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this
58	 * component's own render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape
59	 * — is not built to receive at all).
60	 */
61	import React from 'react';
62	
63	// Chakra Components
64	import { Box, Fade, Flex, Stack, Text, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
65	
66	// Project Components
67	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
68	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
69	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
70	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
71	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
72	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
73	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
74	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
75	import ProductQuantityPicker from './product-quantity-picker';
76	import { ZimmCartItem } from './product-item.css';
77	
78	// Utilities
79	import { noop } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils';
80	
81	// Hooks
82	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
83	
84	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
85	
86	type SfccProduct = any;
87	
88	type ProductItemProps = {
89	  product: SfccProduct;
90	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
91	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
92	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
93	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
94	  /**
95	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
96	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
97	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
98	   */
99	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
100	  showLoading?: boolean;
101	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
102	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
103	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
104	  isRemoving?: boolean;
105	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
106	};
107	
108	/**
109	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
110	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
111	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
112	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
113	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
114	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
115	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
116	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
117	 */
118	const ProductItem = ({
119	  product,
120	  primaryAction,
121	  secondaryActions,
122	  deliveryActions,
123	  onItemQuantityChange = noop,
124	  showLoading = false,
125	  containerStyles = {},
126	  isRemoving = false,
127	  pickupInStore = false,
128	}: ProductItemProps) => {
129	  const { stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
130	    product,
131	    false,
132	    false,
133	    pickupInStore,
134	  );
135	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
136	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, {});
137	  return (
138	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
139	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
140	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
141	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
142	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
143	            <CartItemVariantImage />
144	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
145	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
146	                <Stack spacing={1}>
147	                  <CartItemVariantName />
148	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
149	                  <HideOnDesktop>
150	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
151	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
152	                    </Box>
153	                  </HideOnDesktop>
154	                </Stack>
155	                {deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>}
156	              </Flex>
157	
158	              {deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>}
159	
160	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
161	                <Stack spacing={1}>
162	                  {!(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
163	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
164	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
165	                    ) : (
166	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
167	                        product={product}
168	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
169	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
170	                        quantity={quantity}
171	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
172	                      />
173	                    ))}
174	                </Stack>
175	                <Stack>
176	                  <HideOnMobile>
177	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
178	                  </HideOnMobile>
179	                  <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>
180	                </Stack>
181	              </Flex>
182	
183	              <Box>
184	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
185	                  <Fade in={true}>
186	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
187	                      {inventoryMessage}
188	                    </Text>
189	                  </Fade>
190	                )}
191	              </Box>
192	
193	              {secondaryActions}
194	            </Stack>
195	          </Flex>
196	
197	          <HideOnDesktop>
198	            <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
199	          </HideOnDesktop>
200	        </Stack>
201	      </ItemVariantProvider>
202	    </Box>
203	  );
204	};
205	
206	export default ProductItem;

3	/**
4	 * Co-located recipe for the cart line-item shell (overrides/app/components/product-item).
5	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2) — restyles the copy-first port to the Figma-sourced cart-item spec.
6	 *
7	 * Parts:
8	 *   - `row` — the image + item-details row. Figma: gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align
9	 *     centre desktop / start mobile.
10	 *   - `details` — the column beside the image (name/attrs/price/stepper/actions). Figma:
11	 *     gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile.
12	 *   - `info` — the name + colour/size (+ mobile price) block, paired with the desktop-only
13	 *     delivery-actions slot. Figma: column layout desktop / row + justify-space-between
14	 *     mobile. The mobile values match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly
15	 *     (row, space-between, align flex-end) so nothing changes below `md` — only the desktop
16	 *     column switch is new.
17	 *
18	 * Applied via `sx`, not `__css`: `Flex`/`Stack` (`@chakra-ui/layout`'s `chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs` /
19	 * `chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) each pass their own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/
20	 * `flexDirection`/`gap` as literal props ahead of `{...rest}` in their own render, and
21	 * `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`) merges
22	 * `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — `sx` last, unconditionally winning.
23	 * `__css` sits BELOW a plain component's own baseStyle in that merge, so it would be silently
24	 * outranked by Stack's own `gap` / Flex's own `alignItems` whenever this component sets one —
25	 * confirmed by reading both chunks directly, not assumed. `item-variant.css.ts`'s own docblock
26	 * carries the matching note for its sibling files (image/colourSize/price).
27	 */
28	export const ZimmCartItem = {
29	  parts: ['row', 'details', 'info'],
30	  baseStyle: {
31	    row: {
32	      flexDirection: 'row',
33	      alignItems: 'flex-start',
34	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
35	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
36	        alignItems: 'center',
37	        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px desktop
38	      },
39	    },
40	    details: {
41	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
42	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
43	        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)', // 12px desktop
44	      },
45	    },
46	    info: {
47	      flexDirection: 'row',
48	      justifyContent: 'space-between',
49	      alignItems: 'flex-end',
50	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
51	        flexDirection: 'column',
52	        alignItems: 'flex-start',
53	        justifyContent: 'flex-start',
54	      },
55	    },
56	  },
57	};

9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-image.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotations and a
12	 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
13	 *
14	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
15	 *
16	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec. The outer Box's own literal
17	 * `width="84px" backgroundColor="gray.100"` defaults are gone, replaced by item-variant.css.ts's
18	 * `image` part via `__css` — kept as `__css`, not `sx`, specifically so a caller-supplied
19	 * `width`/`mr` (e.g. order-summary/index.jsx's base, not-yet-overridden
20	 * `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />`) still wins; see that recipe's own docblock for
21	 * why. `{...props}` stays spread last, same defaults-then-spread order as before, still what
22	 * lets that caller-supplied width win. `ratio`'s default changed from `1` to the Figma-confirmed
23	 * 288/432 cart-item image ratio; the inner <Image> now also carries the `img` part's responsive
24	 * objectFit + mix-blend-multiply. Badge styling (Sale/Unavailable) is untouched — no Figma value
25	 * was given for it at this step.
26	 */
27	import React from 'react';
28	import {
29	  AspectRatio,
30	  Box,
31	  Badge,
32	  Image,
33	  useMultiStyleConfig,
34	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
35	import { useItemVariant } from '.';
36	import { FormattedMessage } from 'react-intl';
37	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
38	
39	// See index.tsx's own note on why this is `any` rather than a structural type.
40	type SfccVariant = any;
41	
42	type ItemImageProps = {
43	  imageProps?: Record<string, any>;
44	  ratio?: number;
45	} & Record<string, any>;
46	
47	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItemVariant';
48	
49	// Figma "Image" spec, product-item card (SFCC-270): aspect ratio 288/432, which reduces to 2/3
50	// exactly. Matches the design record's own 132x198 desktop pair exactly (132 * 432/288 = 198);
51	// against the 67x100 mobile pair it lands at 100.5 — half a pixel over the stated 100, the same
52	// class of Figma-rounding gap zimmDrawer.css.ts's WIDTH_XLARGE note already documents for a
53	// different value, not something introduced here.
54	const CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO = 288 / 432;
55	
56	/**
57	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
58	 * main image.
59	 *
60	 * @todo = This component will render a `SALE` badge when the qualifier is available
61	 * on the custom property `c_isSale`. This will need to be expanded upon to handle
62	 * different badge/qualifiers and property names.
63	 */
64	const ItemImage = ({ imageProps, ratio = CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO, ...props }: ItemImageProps) => {
65	  const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant();
66	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE, {});
67	
68	  // We find the 'small' images in the variant's image groups based on variationValues and pick the first one
69	  const image = findImageGroupBy(variant?.imageGroups, {
70	    viewType: 'small',
71	    selectedVariationAttributes: variant?.variationValues,
72	  })?.images?.[0];
73	
74	  return (
75	    <Box __css={styles.image} {...props}>
76	      <AspectRatio ratio={ratio}>
77	        <Box position="relative">
78	          {variant.c_isSale && (
79	            <Badge
80	              position="absolute"
81	              top={0}
82	              left={0}
83	              marginLeft={2}
84	              marginTop={2}
85	              fontSize="10px"
86	              variant="solid"
87	              colorScheme="blue"
88	            >
89	              <FormattedMessage
90	                defaultMessage="Sale"
91	                id="item_image.label.sale"
92	                description="A sale badge placed on top of a product image"
93	              />
94	            </Badge>
95	          )}
96	          {variant.isProductUnavailable && (
97	            <Badge
98	              position="absolute"
99	              top={0}
100	              left={0}
101	              marginLeft={2}
102	              marginTop={2}
103	              fontSize="10px"
104	              variant="solid"
105	              colorScheme="red"
106	            >
107	              <FormattedMessage
108	                defaultMessage="Unavailable"
109	                id="item_image.label.unavailable"
110	                description="A unavailable badge placed on top of a product image"
111	              />
112	            </Badge>
113	          )}
114	
115	          {image && (
116	            <Image
117	              alt={image.alt}
118	              src={`${image.disBaseLink || image.link}`}
119	              ignoreFallback={true}
120	              __css={styles.img}
121	              {...imageProps}
122	            />
123	          )}
124	        </Box>
125	      </AspectRatio>
126	    </Box>
127	  );
128	};
129	
130	export default ItemImage;

14	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.

42	import { Heading } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

48	 * available upon rendering.

51	  const variant = useItemVariant();
52	  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;
53

56	      <Link color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" {...props} to={`/product/${productId}`}>

/*
 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name.jsx
 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotation and a
 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
 *
 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
 * `Link` is not overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing at time of
 * writing), so it stays on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path.
 *
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2), bug fix: base had `<Link {...props} color="black.600" to={...}>` —
 * spreading `props` BEFORE the explicit `color`/`to`, the opposite order from item-image/
 * item-attributes/item-price's own `{...props}` placement (spread last), so a caller-supplied
 * `color` was silently overridden here instead of taking precedence, unlike those three
 * siblings. Fixed by moving `color` ahead of the spread, matching the siblings' order — `to`
 * stays after the spread, unchanged, since it is data-derived (from `productId`) and was never
 * meant to be caller-overridable the way `color` is. No current base caller passes `color`, so
 * nothing observable changes for them; this only matters going forward.
 *
 * Also restyled per the Figma cart-item spec: `fontSize="md"` (a bare Chakra token — this
 * repo's own `fontSizes` scale is deliberately NOT registered as `theme.fontSizes`, see
 * typography.ts, so that literal was silently reading Chakra's own unrelated default) replaced
 * by `textStyle="productNames"`, which also carries the spec's "uppercase" requirement (see
 * typography.ts's `productNames` entry). The bug-fixed default colour is expressed as a literal
 * `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` prop rather than routed through the recipe: a plain literal
 * prop is provably override-safe here regardless of `Link`'s own internal implementation (it
 * lands in the same `props` bucket a caller's own `color` would use), where `__css`/`sx` on this
 * specific base `Link` wrapper is not — see item-variant.css.ts's own docblock for the
 * `__css`-discarding hazard that rules `__css` out for a plain Chakra `Text`, a nearby but
 * distinct case worth being equally careful about here.
 */
import React from 'react';
import { useItemVariant } from '.';
import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
import { Heading } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

/**
 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this components simply renders
 * the item's name using the cart item field `productName`. We use this field
 * rather than variant `name` field as the variant detail may not yet be
 * available upon rendering.
 */
const ItemName = (props: Record<string, any>) => {
  const variant = useItemVariant();
  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;

  return (
    <Heading as="h2" textStyle="productNames">
      <Link color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" {...props} to={`/product/${productId}`}>
        {variant.productName || variant.name}
      </Link>

};

13	/**
14	 * Co-located recipe for the item-variant family (item-image / item-attributes / item-price).
15	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2).
16	 *
17	 * Parts:
18	 *   - `image` — item-image.tsx's outer Box: responsive width, ivory-200 background. Applied
19	 *     via `__css`, not `sx` — this one MUST stay overridable: order-summary/index.jsx (base
20	 *     SFCC, not yet overridden in this repo) calls
21	 *     `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` and depends on its own caller-supplied
22	 *     `width` winning over whatever default this component ships. `__css` is the lowest-
23	 *     priority slot in `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` merge (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`:
24	 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)`), and `Box` carries no competing
25	 *     baseStyle of its own (`@chakra-ui/layout`'s `chunk-6CSUKJP7.mjs`: `var Box =
26	 *     chakra("div")`, no options) — confirmed by reading both files, not assumed — so a
27	 *     literal caller prop always wins over this part's `__css` default.
28	 *   - `img` — the inner <Image>: responsive objectFit (contain mobile / cover desktop) plus
29	 *     mix-blend-multiply, so the photo blends against the `image` part's ivory backdrop.
30	 *     `__css` is safe here too — Chakra's own `Image` (`@chakra-ui/image`'s
31	 *     `chunk-SMHKDLMK.mjs`) never sets a literal `__css` key of its own, unlike `Text` below.
32	 *   - `colourSize` — item-attributes.tsx's combined "colour, size" string.
33	 *   - `price` — item-price.tsx's price Stack (`textStyle: 'price'` only; the actual price
34	 *     digits render via the base, un-overridden `display-price`/`current-price` components,
35	 *     which set no competing font-size of their own — confirmed by reading both files — so
36	 *     the textStyle cascades down via ordinary CSS inheritance without touching either file).

39	 * (`@chakra-ui/layout`'s `chunk-P74GIWPW.mjs`) places its OWN `__css={styles}` (from

41	 * a caller-supplied `__css` prop would be silently discarded entirely there (a later

5	// file previously guessed at. Each name below matches Figma's own naming exactly, so there's
6	// no re-deriving which number belongs to which concept next time this file is touched:
7	//

9	//   Tablet        — 80%  — Product Details, Filters (tablet width)
10	//   Desktop Small — 25%  — Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, Regional Storefront,
11	//                           Cookies, Login
12	//   X-Large       — 82%  — Cart. SFCC-11: this is the named-size *library* annotation, not a
13	//                           measurement of the real Cart composition — see `WIDTH_XLARGE` below,
14	//                           which corrects it a second time against the actual frames.
15	//   Mobile        — unchanged, the baseStyle treatment every variant collapses to below `md`.
16	//
17	// An earlier revision of this file measured 82% off a Figma frame annotated "Tablet = 82% of
18	// screen" and used it as `small`'s (now `tablet`'s) value — that frame's annotation was wrong
19	// (or superseded): 82% is actually X-Large's value (Cart), a completely different drawer this
20	// codebase hasn't built yet, and Tablet is genuinely 80%. Corrected once confirmed directly
21	// against the list above, not another single frame's own label.
22	const WIDTH_LARGE = '50%';
23	const WIDTH_TABLET = '80%';
24	// The original width set when this drawer shell was first built (2026-08-27) — matches Figma's
25	// "Desktop Small" exactly. Used by every viewport-independent narrow utility drawer (Find in
26	// Boutique today; Notify Me/Wishlist/Regional Storefront/Cookies/Login once those exist).
27	const WIDTH_SMALL = '25%';

16	import CartItemVariantImage from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-image'
17	import CartItemVariantName from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name'

19	import CartItemVariantPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'
20	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner'
21	import BonusProductQuantity from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/bonus-product-quantity'

26	
27	// Hooks
28	import {useCurrency, useDerivedProduct} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks'
29	
30	/**
31	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
32	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
33	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
34	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
35	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
36	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
37	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
38	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
39	 */
40	const ProductItem = ({
41	    product,
42	    primaryAction,
43	    secondaryActions,
44	    deliveryActions,
45	    onItemQuantityChange = noop,
46	    showLoading = false,
47	    containerStyles = {},
48	    isRemoving = false,
49	    pickupInStore = false
50	}) => {
51	    const {stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity} =
52	        useDerivedProduct(product, false, false, pickupInStore)
53	    const {currency: activeCurrency} = useCurrency()
54	    return (
55	        <Box
56	            position="relative"
57	            data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}
58	        >
59	            <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
60	                {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
61	                <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
62	                    <Flex width="full" alignItems="flex-start" backgroundColor="white">
63	                        <CartItemVariantImage width={['88px', '136px']} mr={4} />
64	                        <Stack spacing={3} flex={1}>
65	                            <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
66	                                <Stack spacing={1}>
67	                                    <CartItemVariantName />
68	                                    <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel />
69	                                    <HideOnDesktop>
70	                                        <Box marginTop={2}>
71	                                            <CartItemVariantPrice
72	                                                align="left"
73	                                                currency={activeCurrency}
74	                                            />
75	                                        </Box>
76	                                    </HideOnDesktop>
77	                                </Stack>
78	                                {deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
79	                                    <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
80	                                )}
81	                            </Flex>
82	
83	                            {deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
84	                                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
85	                            )}
86	
87	                            <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
88	                                <Stack spacing={1}>
89	                                    {!(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
90	                                        (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
91	                                            <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
92	                                        ) : (
93	                                            <ProductQuantityPicker
94	                                                product={product}
95	                                                onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
96	                                                stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
97	                                                quantity={quantity}
98	                                                setQuantity={setQuantity}
99	                                            />
100	                                        ))}
101	                                </Stack>
102	                                <Stack>
103	                                    <HideOnMobile>
104	                                        <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
105	                                    </HideOnMobile>
106	                                    <Box display={['none', 'block', 'block', 'block']}>
107	                                        {primaryAction}
108	                                    </Box>
109	                                </Stack>
110	                            </Flex>
111	
112	                            <Box>
113	                                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
114	                                    <Fade in={true}>
115	                                        <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
116	                                            {inventoryMessage}
117	                                        </Text>
118	                                    </Fade>
119	                                )}
120	                            </Box>
121	
122	                            {secondaryActions}
123	                        </Stack>
124	                    </Flex>
125	
126	                    <Box display={['block', 'none', 'none', 'none']} w={'full'}>
127	                        {primaryAction}
128	                    </Box>
129	                </Stack>
130	            </ItemVariantProvider>
131	        </Box>
132	    )
133	}
134	
135	ProductItem.propTypes = {
136	    product: PropTypes.object,
137	    onItemQuantityChange: PropTypes.func,
138	    onAddItemToCart: PropTypes.func,
139	    showLoading: PropTypes.bool,
140	    isWishlistItem: PropTypes.bool,

142	    secondaryActions: PropTypes.node,
143	    deliveryActions: PropTypes.node,
144	    containerStyles: PropTypes.object,
145	    isRemoving: PropTypes.bool,
146	    pickupInStore: PropTypes.bool
147	}

 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
 */
const ProductItem = ({
    product,
    primaryAction,
    secondaryActions,
    deliveryActions,
    onItemQuantityChange = noop,
    showLoading = false,
    containerStyles = {},
    isRemoving = false,
    pickupInStore = false
}) => {
    const {stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity} =
        useDerivedProduct(product, false, false, pickupInStore)
    const {currency: activeCurrency} = useCurrency()
    return (
        <Box
            position="relative"
            data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}
        >
            <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
                {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
                <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
                    <Flex width="full" alignItems="flex-start" backgroundColor="white">
                        <CartItemVariantImage width={['88px', '136px']} mr={4} />
                        <Stack spacing={3} flex={1}>
                            <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                                <Stack spacing={1}>
                                    <CartItemVariantName />
                                    <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel />
                                    <HideOnDesktop>
                                        <Box marginTop={2}>
                                            <CartItemVariantPrice
                                                align="left"
                                                currency={activeCurrency}
                                            />
                                        </Box>
                                    </HideOnDesktop>
                                </Stack>
                                {deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                                    <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
                                )}
                            </Flex>

                            {deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
                            )}

                            <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                                <Stack spacing={1}>
                                    {!(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
                                        (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
                                            <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
                                        ) : (
                                            <ProductQuantityPicker
                                                product={product}
                                                onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
                                                stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
                                                quantity={quantity}
                                                setQuantity={setQuantity}
                                            />
                                        ))}
                                </Stack>
                                <Stack>
                                    <HideOnMobile>
                                        <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
                                    </HideOnMobile>
                                    <Box display={['none', 'block', 'block', 'block']}>
                                        {primaryAction}
                                    </Box>
                                </Stack>
                            </Flex>

                            <Box>
                                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
                                    <Fade in={true}>
                                        <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
                                            {inventoryMessage}
                                        </Text>
                                    </Fade>
                                )}
                            </Box>

                            {secondaryActions}
                        </Stack>
                    </Flex>

                    <Box display={['block', 'none', 'none', 'none']} w={'full'}>
                        {primaryAction}
                    </Box>
                </Stack>
            </ItemVariantProvider>
        </Box>
    )
}

ProductItem.propTypes = {
    product: PropTypes.object,
    onItemQuantityChange: PropTypes.func,
    onAddItemToCart: PropTypes.func,
    showLoading: PropTypes.bool,
    isWishlistItem: PropTypes.bool,
    primaryAction: PropTypes.node,
    secondaryActions: PropTypes.node,
    deliveryActions: PropTypes.node,
    containerStyles: PropTypes.object,
    isRemoving: PropTypes.bool,
    pickupInStore: PropTypes.bool
}

export default ProductItem

Scope note: session-notes.md's own 9-AC list (line 299-301) matches exactly what was given to me — no more-current version found. Used `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2 (CAI-006–017) as the underlying PRD source and `.docs/prd/giftcards.md` for the gift-card cross-check.

## AC-by-AC (evidence-based)

**AC1 — image: PASS (CONFIRMED).** `item-image.tsx:74-127` renders `<Image alt={image.alt} .../>` inside an `AspectRatio`; ratio changed to `288/432` (`item-image.tsx:54`). Alt text present, no truncation/hiding.

**AC2 — name to the right of the image: PASS (CONFIRMED).** `product-item/index.tsx:142-144`: `<Flex sx={styles.row}>` renders `<CartItemVariantImage />` (line 143) then `<Stack sx={styles.details}>` containing `<CartItemVariantName />` (line 147) — image first, name second, in document order. `product-item.css.ts:31-39`'s `row` part sets `flexDirection: 'row'` unconditionally (mobile default, unchanged at the `md` breakpoint — only `alignItems`/`gap` change at line 35-38) — confirmed at both mobile and desktop, image precedes name in a row-direction flex.

**AC3 — price: PASS (CONFIRMED).** `<CartItemVariantPrice>` renders twice: mobile inside `HideOnDesktop` (`product-item/index.tsx:149-153`), desktop inside `HideOnMobile` (`:176-178`). `item-price.tsx` restyled via `textStyle: 'price'` (`item-variant.css.ts:80-82`).

**AC4+AC5 — colour, size: PASS as "two ACs, one element" (CONFIRMED, and confirmed session-notes.md blesses this).** `session-notes.md:725-727` explicitly records: *"colour + size: ONE combined string ('Lilac Sand, One size')... (SFCC-270 has separate ACs for colour and for size — two ACs, one element)"* — this is a real, pre-recorded design decision, not the Implementer inventing scope reduction. Code: `item-attributes.tsx:147-149` — `{variationValues && combineAttributeValues && (<Text sx={styles.colourSize}>{Object.values(variationValues).join(', ')}</Text>)}` — this is unambiguously **one** `<Text>` node containing one joined string, not two elements styled adjacent (confirmed by direct JSX read, not inference). Old per-key branch (`:151-157`) is preserved, gated by `!combineAttributeValues`, so no regression for other callers. Test assertion `product-item/index.test.tsx:155` (`getByText('Lilac Sand, One size')`) is a meaningful check, not a false-positive: Testing Library's `getByText` matches via `getNodeText`, which concatenates only an element's **direct** text-node children (not `.textContent`, which would recursively include nested elements) — so if the value were split across two sibling `<Text>`s instead, no single node would match this exact string and the test would fail. (This mechanism claim is PLAUSIBLE/reasoned from documented Testing-Library behaviour, not re-run by me — another agent covers actually executing the suite.)

**AC6 — quantity with +/- either side: PASS, structurally unbroken (CONFIRMED, out of this commit's logic scope as expected).** `product-quantity-picker.tsx` is untouched this commit (not in `git status`'s M list) and wraps the base `QuantityPicker` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/quantity-picker/index.jsx:104-114`), which renders `<HStack><Button data-testid="quantity-decrement">−</Button><Input .../><Button data-testid="quantity-increment">+</Button></HStack>` — value structurally flanked by decrement/increment. This commit's restyle doesn't touch this file or the `<Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">` row it sits in (`product-item/index.tsx:160-174`) beyond the surrounding container's spacing tokens, so the stepper's own DOM shape is unaffected. Mutation/debounce logic is SFCC-271 per `session-notes.md` (separate ticket, matches task framing).

**AC7 — multiple items individually identifiable: shopper-facing PASS, but a real internal-identifier weakness exists (CONFIRMED via SDK types + this repo's own prior research, not reproduced live).**
- `product-item/index.tsx:138`: `data-testid={\`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}\`}` keys off `productId`/`id`.
- `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:6968-7011` (`ProductItem` type): `itemId` is documented *"The product item ID. Use it to identify this item when updating its quantity..."* (i.e., the SDK's own canonical per-line identifier) while `productId` is documented only as *"The ID of the product"* — no uniqueness claim, and it's the shared SKU id.
- This repo's own `session-notes.md:104-116` (§2.3, basket-merge research) already documents that two basket lines with the **same `productId`** legitimately coexist as separate lines whenever they differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag / option values / wishlist reference — and explicitly names **Collect-in-Boutique (separate shipment)** and **boutique-vs-warehouse inventory list** as realistic Zimmermann scenarios for this. A `bonusProductLineItem` vs. a regular line of the same product is another plausible same-`productId` case already handled elsewhere in this very file (`product.bonusProductLineItem` branches at `:155,158,162-173`).
- Internal inconsistency: this same commit already uses `itemId` as the "is this a real basket line" signal elsewhere (`item-price.tsx:91,123`: `variant?.itemId ? ... : /* wishlist page */`), but the identifying `data-testid` does not use it.
- Net effect: two distinct cart line items sharing a `productId` would render **identical** `data-testid`s — an automation/testability gap (E2E selectors, analytics keyed off this attribute), not necessarily a shopper-visible failure, since the rows still differ on quantity/price/other rendered fields in most cases. Neither `index.test.tsx` nor `index.stories.tsx`'s `MultipleItems` story (which uses two *different* `productId`s, `25595021M`/`25601452M`) exercises the same-`productId` case, so nothing in the existing suite would catch this. I did not render a live basket to see two colliding nodes side by side — this is reasoned from the SDK type + this repo's own documented merge rules, which I judge strong enough to call CONFIRMED-by-evidence per the task's own definition for this checkpoint ("a real basket shape where two lines can share productId"), while flagging it wasn't literally reproduced in a browser/test.

**AC8 — Remove/Wishlist as underlined links below the stepper: OUT OF SCOPE for this commit, correctly (CONFIRMED).** `session-notes.md:33` lists **SFCC-272 "Cart Item – Remove and Wishlist Actions"** as its own ticket (8 ACs, `:419-428`), separate from SFCC-270. In this commit's code, `primaryAction` renders via `<HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>` (`product-item/index.tsx:179`) and `<Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>` (`:198`); `secondaryActions` renders bare at `:193`. Neither gets any styling (no underline, no `ZimmLink`, no `textDecoration`, no colour) applied **by this file** — both are opaque `React.ReactNode` slots, exactly as the task expected. Nothing in this commit would block SFCC-272 from styling them correctly later (no conflicting resets found in `product-item.css.ts`'s `row`/`details`/`info` parts). Literal AC-8 text is not satisfied *by this commit*, but per the ticket-boundary evidence, that's correctly out of scope here, not a gap in SFCC-270.

**AC9 — mobile nothing truncated/hidden: code-level PASS, tooling-capability claim CONFIRMED (both from source only).**
- Grepped all 6 changed files (`item-attributes.tsx`, `item-image.tsx`, `item-name.tsx`, `item-price.tsx`, `item-variant.css.ts`, `product-item.css.ts`, plus `product-item/index.tsx`) for `noOfLines|isTruncated|text-overflow|textOverflow|overflow.*hidden|display.*none` — **zero matches**. No new truncation/hiding CSS introduced.
- One residual risk worth flagging for the live-render agent (not something I can resolve from source): `item-variant.css.ts:11,77` fixes `COLOUR_SIZE_WIDTH = '200px'` on the combined colour+size string at all breakpoints, including the 67px-wide mobile image column. A long combined string would **wrap**, not truncate/hide (no `noOfLines`/`isTruncated` present) — so it wouldn't violate the literal AC wording, but could look cramped at 402px. Flagging, not claiming a failure.
- Tooling-capability claim, checked directly: `vitest.config.ts`'s `test.include` is `['overrides/**/*.test.ts', 'overrides/**/*.test.tsx']` only — `.stories.tsx` files are never run by Vitest (and are explicitly excluded even from coverage, `vitest.config.ts` coverage.exclude). `.storybook/main.js`'s `addons` array is `['@storybook/addon-webpack5-compiler-babel', '@storybook/addon-links', '@storybook/addon-docs', '@storybook/addon-a11y']` — no `@storybook/addon-viewport`, no `addon-essentials`. **CONFIRMED as a factual tooling statement:** this repo's Vitest/Storybook setup cannot mechanically render or assert against a 402px viewport today; a real browser (Playwright) is genuinely required for this AC, matching the Implementer's claim.

## Gift-card suppression re-verification (independent, wider search)

1. **SDK type separation — CONFIRMED.** `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:6282` declares `type GiftCertificateItem = { amount: number; giftCertificateItemId?: string; message?: string; recipientEmail: string; recipientName?: string; senderName?: string; shipmentId?: string } & {[key:string]: any}` — no `productId`, no `imageGroups`, no `variationValues`/`variationAttributes`, no `price`/`quantity` fields `ProductItem`'s render tree depends on. The `Basket` type carries it as a **sibling, separate** array field: `giftCertificateItems?: Array<GiftCertificateItem>` (`:7071`) vs. `productItems?: Array<ProductItem>` (`:7078`) — confirmed adjacent, structurally disjoint.
2. **Base retail-react-app never renders it — CONFIRMED.** `grep -rln "GiftCertificate|giftCertificate" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` returned **zero files**. `order-summary/index.jsx:37-38,78` only ever reads `basket.productItems` (`totalItems`, `productIds`, and the render map) — never `basket.giftCertificateItems`. The base cart page directory exists but nothing in it references gift certificates either (same zero-match grep covers it). Base retail-react-app v10.0.0 simply has no gift-certificate basket-line rendering built anywhere.
3. **No existing artifact in this repo either — CONFIRMED.** `grep -rln "giftCard|GiftCard|giftCertificate|GiftCertificate" overrides/` returns only the two files that are part of *this same commit's own disclosure* (`product-item/index.tsx`'s docblock, `index.stories.tsx`'s docblock) — no pre-existing type, constant, or component anywhere else.
4. **PRD cross-check reinforces this is a genuinely different rendering, not just an unrouted data type.** `.docs/prd/giftcards.md` §4 (`:38-51`) specifies gift cards in cart render a **different field set entirely** — sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, personal message (digital), Edit action (digital-only, no Edit for physical) — not a variant of image/name/colour/size/quantity/Remove+Wishlist that `ProductItem` implements. `session-notes.md:650-651,672-674` independently confirms gift cards are "outside the 7" ACs bundled into this cart epic and belong to a wholly separate "Gift Cards / Credit Notes epic, Sprint 6."

**Conclusion: REFUTED that anything was missed — this is a genuine, correctly-disclosed gap, nothing to build against today.** There is no real signal `ProductItem` could branch on, and base retail-react-app itself never had this capability to inherit.

**One nuance the Implementer's docblock doesn't address, worth surfacing.** `session-notes.md:737-740` (Figma §11.2, same-day dated 2026-09-16) separately records: *"Gift card variant (out of scope, but the component API must allow it)... build `ZimmCartItem` with the stepper and actions row **optional**"* — a forward-compatibility requirement distinct from "is there a data signal today." The actual DECIDED architecture (`session-notes.md:303`, also 2026-09-16) supersedes the `ZimmCartItem`-wrapper idea in favour of overriding base `product-item` directly, and this commit's docblock never cites or reconciles the §11.2 "must allow it" note. Having read the shipped code, I don't see anything that structurally forecloses adding an optional gift-card branch later — `primaryAction`/`secondaryActions` are already caller-supplied optional nodes, and the file already demonstrates a conditional-stepper pattern via `product.bonusProductLineItem` (`:155,158,162-173`) that a future gift-card flag could extend the same way. So I don't think the forward-compatibility requirement was violated — but it also wasn't explicitly checked off, and the docblock's silence on it is a documentation gap, not just a data-signal gap. (This paragraph is PLAUSIBLE/my own downstream assessment, not something I tested by actually adding such a prop.)

## Three judgment calls

**(a) "Item Info" grouping mapped onto existing structure — reasonable, with one nuance not fully verifiable from source.** `product-item.css.ts:12-16`'s own docblock states the mobile values "match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly... only the desktop column switch is new." Confirmed by reading `product-item.css.ts:46-55` (`info` part: row/justify-space-between on mobile unconditionally close to base's own original layout, column on desktop only via the `md` media query) — a minimal, additive change. One thing I could **not** fully verify: `session-notes.md:719`'s Figma table lists desktop "Item Info" as `flex-col, name above price` — but in the actual code, the **desktop** price is not inside the `info` Flex at all; it renders separately in the stepper row's own `Stack` alongside `primaryAction` (`product-item/index.tsx:175-180`), not directly under the name. Visually the name/attrs still sit above the stepper row overall (so "name above price" holds loosely, top-to-bottom), but they are not literally grouped in one shared flex the Figma label implies. This is a Figma-fidelity nuance, not a violation of any of the 9 numbered Jira ACs (none require price to be nested directly under name) — flagging for awareness, not as a failure. I have no Figma access in this task's scope to check the frame directly, so I can't go further than this.

**(b) Unified mobile/desktop split to `md`/768px — CONFIRMED reasonable, and the underlying facts check out.** `gridSystem.ts:12-19` (`breakpoints`) confirms `md: '48em'` (768px), and this exact object (not just similarly-valued) is registered onto the real Chakra theme via `theme/index.ts:53`. Independently read the **base** `product-item/index.jsx:106,126` to confirm the claim about the original arrays: `display={['none','block','block','block']}` and `display={['block','none','none','none']}` are 4-element Chakra responsive arrays, which — mapped against this project's own registered `breakpoints` object (`base:0em, sm:30em/480px, md:48em/768px, lg:62em/992px,...`, `gridSystem.ts:12-19`, identical in value to Chakra's stock defaults) — resolve to a **480px (`sm`)** split, exactly as the docblock claims (I verified this against the base source directly, not by trusting the comment). `responsive/index.tsx:12` (`MOBILE_DESKTOP_SPLIT = 'md'`) is a **pre-existing** override (unmodified this commit, already used site-wide for header/footer/mega-menu per its own docblock `:5-9`), so replacing the two ad-hoc 480px arrays with the file's own already-imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` is consolidating onto an established, already-battle-tested convention rather than inventing a new one. This is reasonable engineering judgment, disclosed prominently in the docblock ("flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a tested requirement") — though it is a real, if narrow, behavioural change (in the 480–768px band, `primaryAction`'s visibility toggle now flips at a different point than before), and it touches the visibility logic of the exact slot (`primaryAction`) that SFCC-272 will build into — worth a one-line awareness flag for the reviewer even though I judge it reasonable, not a scope overstep.

**(c) Image aspect ratio 288/432 → 100.5px mobile height — the value itself is fine; the cited precedent is not accurate.** `item-image.tsx:49-53`'s docblock claims the 100.5px-vs-100px half-pixel gap is *"the same class of Figma-rounding gap zimmDrawer.css.ts's `WIDTH_XLARGE` note already documents for a different value."* I read `zimmDrawer.css.ts:4-39` in full: that note is **not** about a rounding/precision remainder from ratio math at all — it documents a **wrong-annotation-vs-real-measurement** correction (an "X-Large = 82%" library annotation was actually mislabeled — the real Cart frame is a **fixed** 1186px, not a percentage, and separately a *different* wrong 82% figure had been mistakenly used for `Tablet`, which is genuinely 80%). That's a categorical labelling/measurement error, corrected by re-measuring real Figma frames — a different kind of problem from "67 × 432/288 = 100.5, half a pixel over a stated round number," which is a benign, unavoidable arithmetic consequence of applying one exact ratio (288/432, which is exact for the 132×198 desktop pair) to a second dimension pair that wasn't itself perfectly divisible. **CONFIRMED: this is not the same class of gap as claimed** — the citation is inaccurate, even though the underlying 100.5px value itself is not a bug (it's the mathematically correct result of the stated ratio, and half a pixel is visually immaterial). This is a documentation-precision issue in the docblock's justification, not a functional defect.

## What I could not verify, and why

- **Any live/visual rendering** (does the combined colour+size text actually wrap or look cramped at 402px; does the "Item Info" desktop layout visually read as "name above price" per Figma) — explicitly out of my lane; another agent is doing real-browser/Playwright measurement.
- **Whether `npm run test` / the Vitest suite actually passes** for `index.test.tsx`/`item-variant/index.test.tsx` — I read the test files and reasoned about their assertions' rigor (e.g. the `getByText` single-node semantics) from documented Testing-Library behaviour, but did not execute them myself; another agent covers compile/tests.
- **The literal Figma "Item Info" frame** for judgment call (a) — I have no Figma access in this task's scope; my read is code-only, cross-checked only against `session-notes.md`'s own textual transcription of the frame, not the frame itself.
- **A live two-line-same-`productId` basket** for AC7 — reasoned from the SDK type contract and this repo's own prior documented basket-merge research, not reproduced by actually adding two such lines to a running basket.
- **Whether the `ZimmCartItem`-optional-stepper forward-compatibility note (`session-notes.md:737-740`) was actively considered and consciously deferred**, vs. simply not found during the Implementer's search — I can only observe the docblock doesn't mention it; I can't determine intent from the artifact alone.

- `product-item/index.tsx:138`: `data-testid={\`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}\`}` keys off `productId`/`id`.
- `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:6968-7011` (`ProductItem` type): `itemId` is documented *"The product item ID. Use it to identify this item when updating its quantity..."* (i.e., the SDK's own canonical per-line identifier) while `productId` is documented only as *"The ID of the product"* — no uniqueness claim, and it's the shared SKU id.
- This repo's own `session-notes.md:104-116` (§2.3, basket-merge research) already documents that two basket lines with the **same `productId`** legitimately coexist as separate lines whenever they differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag / option values / wishlist reference — and explicitly names **Collect-in-Boutique (separate shipment)** and **boutique-vs-warehouse inventory list** as realistic Zimmermann scenarios for this. A `bonusProductLineItem` vs. a regular line of the same product is another plausible same-`productId` case already handled elsewhere in this very file (`product.bonusProductLineItem` branches at `:155,158,162-173`).
- Internal inconsistency: this same commit already uses `itemId` as the "is this a real basket line" signal elsewhere (`item-price.tsx:91,123`: `variant?.itemId ? ... : /* wishlist page */`), but the identifying `data-testid` does not use it.
- Net effect: two distinct cart line items sharing a `productId` would render **identical** `data-testid`s — an automation/testability gap (E2E selectors, analytics keyed off this attribute), not necessarily a shopper-visible failure, since the rows still differ on quantity/price/other rendered fields in most cases. Neither `index.test.tsx` nor `index.stories.tsx`'s `MultipleItems` story (which uses two *different* `productId`s, `25595021M`/`25601452M`) exercises the same-`productId` case, so nothing in the existing suite would catch this. I did not render a live basket to see two colliding nodes side by side — this is reasoned from the SDK type + this repo's own documented merge rules, which I judge strong enough to call CONFIRMED-by-evidence per the task's own definition for this checkpoint ("a real basket shape where two lines can share productId"), while flagging it wasn't literally reproduced in a browser/test.

**AC8 — Remove/Wishlist as underlined links below the stepper: OUT OF SCOPE for this commit, correctly (CONFIRMED).** `session-notes.md:33` lists **SFCC-272 "Cart Item – Remove and Wishlist Actions"** as its own ticket (8 ACs, `:419-428`), separate from SFCC-270. In this commit's code, `primaryAction` renders via `<HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>` (`product-item/index.tsx:179`) and `<Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>` (`:198`); `secondaryActions` renders bare at `:193`. Neither gets any styling (no underline, no `ZimmLink`, no `textDecoration`, no colour) applied **by this file** — both are opaque `React.ReactNode` slots, exactly as the task expected. Nothing in this commit would block SFCC-272 from styling them correctly later (no conflicting resets found in `product-item.css.ts`'s `row`/`details`/`info` parts). **AC9 — mobile nothing truncated/hidden: code-level PASS, tooling-capability claim CONFIRMED (both from source only).**
- Grepped all 6 changed files (`item-attributes.tsx`, `item-image.tsx`, `item-name.tsx`, `item-price.tsx`, `item-variant.css.ts`, `product-item.css.ts`, plus `product-item/index.tsx`) for `noOfLines|isTruncated|text-overflow|textOverflow|overflow.*hidden|display.*none` — **zero matches**. A long combined string would **wrap**, not truncate/hide (no `noOfLines`/`isTruncated` present) — so it wouldn't violate the literal AC wording, but could look cramped at 402px.
