## Gift-card suppression re-verification (independent, wider search)

1. **SDK type separation — CONFIRMED.** `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:6282` declares `type GiftCertificateItem = { amount: number; giftCertificateItemId?: string; message?: string; recipientEmail: string; recipientName?: string; senderName?: string; shipmentId?: string } & {[key:string]: any}` — no `productId`, no `imageGroups`, no `variationValues`/`variationAttributes`, no `price`/`quantity` fields `ProductItem`'s render tree depends on. The `Basket` type carries it as a **sibling, separate** array field: `giftCertificateItems?: Array<GiftCertificateItem>` (`:7071`) vs. `productItems?: Array<ProductItem>` (`:7078`) — confirmed adjacent, structurally disjoint.
2. **Base retail-react-app never renders it — CONFIRMED.** `grep -rln "GiftCertificate|giftCertificate" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` returned **zero files**. `order-summary/index.jsx:37-38,78` only ever reads `basket.productItems` (`totalItems`, `productIds`, and the render map) — never `basket.giftCertificateItems`. The base cart page directory exists but nothing in it references gift certificates either (same zero-match grep covers it). Base retail-react-app v10.0.0 simply has no gift-certificate basket-line rendering built anywhere.
3. **No existing artifact in this repo either — CONFIRMED.** `grep -rln "giftCard|GiftCard|giftCertificate|GiftCertificate" overrides/` returns only the two files that are part of *this same commit's own disclosure* (`product-item/index.tsx`'s docblock, `index.stories.tsx`'s docblock) — no pre-existing type, constant, or component anywhere else.
4. **PRD cross-check reinforces this is a genuinely different rendering, not just an unrouted data type.** `.docs/prd/giftcards.md` §4 (`:38-51`) specifies gift cards in cart render a **different field set entirely** — sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, personal message (digital), Edit action (digital-only, no Edit for physical) — not a variant of image/name/colour/size/quantity/Remove+Wishlist that `ProductItem` implements. `session-notes.md:650-651,672-674` independently confirms gift cards are "outside the 7" ACs bundled into this cart epic and belong to a wholly separate "Gift Cards / Credit Notes epic, Sprint 6."

**Conclusion: REFUTED that anything was missed — this is a genuine, correctly-disclosed gap, nothing to build against today.** There is no real signal `ProductItem` could branch on, and base retail-react-app itself never had this capability to inherit.

**One nuance the Implementer's docblock doesn't address, worth surfacing.** `session-notes.md:737-740` (Figma §11.2, same-day dated 2026-09-16) separately records: *"Gift card variant (out of scope, but the component API must allow it)... build `ZimmCartItem` with the stepper and actions row **optional**"* — a forward-compatibility requirement distinct from "is there a data signal today." The actual DECIDED architecture (`session-notes.md:303`, also 2026-09-16) supersedes the `ZimmCartItem`-wrapper idea in favour of overriding base `product-item` directly, and this commit's docblock never cites or reconciles the §11.2 "must allow it" note. Having read the shipped code, I don't see anything that structurally forecloses adding an optional gift-card branch later — `primaryAction`/`secondaryActions` are already caller-supplied optional nodes, and the file already demonstrates a conditional-stepper pattern via `product.bonusProductLineItem` (`:155,158,162-173`) that a future gift-card flag could extend the same way. So I don't think the forward-compatibility requirement was violated — but it also wasn't explicitly checked off, and the docblock's silence on it is a documentation gap, not just a data-signal gap. (This paragraph is PLAUSIBLE/my own downstream assessment, not something I tested by actually adding such a prop.)

## Three judgment calls

**(a) "Item Info" grouping mapped onto existing structure — reasonable, with one nuance not fully verifiable from source.** `product-item.css.ts:12-16`'s own docblock states the mobile values "match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly... only the desktop column switch is new." Confirmed by reading `product-item.css.ts:46-55` (`info` part: row/justify-space-between on mobile unconditionally close to base's own original layout, column on desktop only via the `md` media query) — a minimal, additive change. One thing I could **not** fully verify: `session-notes.md:719`'s Figma table lists desktop "Item Info" as `flex-col, name above price` — but in the actual code, the **desktop** price is not inside the `info` Flex at all; it renders separately in the stepper row's own `Stack` alongside `primaryAction` (`product-item/index.tsx:175-180`), not directly under the name. Visually the name/attrs still sit above the stepper row overall (so "name above price" holds loosely, top-to-bottom), but they are not literally grouped in one shared flex the Figma label implies. This is a Figma-fidelity nuance, not a violation of any of the 9 numbered Jira ACs (none require price to be nested directly under name) — flagging for awareness, not as a failure. I have no Figma access in this task's scope to check the frame directly, so I can't go further than this.

**(b) Unified mobile/desktop split to `md`/768px — CONFIRMED reasonable, and the underlying facts check out.** `gridSystem.ts:12-19` (`breakpoints`) confirms `md: '48em'` (768px), and this exact object (not just similarly-valued) is registered onto the real Chakra theme via `theme/index.ts:53`. Independently read the **base** `product-item/index.jsx:106,126` to confirm the claim about the original arrays: `display={['none','block','block','block']}` and `display={['block','none','none','none']}` are 4-element Chakra responsive arrays, which — mapped against this project's own registered `breakpoints` object (`base:0em, sm:30em/480px, md:48em/768px, lg:62em/992px,...`, `gridSystem.ts:12-19`, identical in value to Chakra's stock defaults) — resolve to a **480px (`sm`)** split, exactly as the docblock claims (I verified this against the base source directly, not by trusting the comment). `responsive/index.tsx:12` (`MOBILE_DESKTOP_SPLIT = 'md'`) is a **pre-existing** override (unmodified this commit, already used site-wide for header/footer/mega-menu per its own docblock `:5-9`), so replacing the two ad-hoc 480px arrays with the file's own already-imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` is consolidating onto an established, already-battle-tested convention rather than inventing a new one. This is reasonable engineering judgment, disclosed prominently in the docblock ("flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a tested requirement") — though it is a real, if narrow, behavioural change (in the 480–768px band, `primaryAction`'s visibility toggle now flips at a different point than before), and it touches the visibility logic of the exact slot (`primaryAction`) that SFCC-272 will build into — worth a one-line awareness flag for the reviewer even though I judge it reasonable, not a scope overstep.

**(c) Image aspect ratio 288/432 → 100.5px mobile height — the value itself is fine; the cited precedent is not accurate.** `item-image.tsx:49-53`'s docblock claims the 100.5px-vs-100px half-pixel gap is *"the same class of Figma-rounding gap zimmDrawer.css.ts's `WIDTH_XLARGE` note already documents for a different value."* I read `zimmDrawer.css.ts:4-39` in full: that note is **not** about a rounding/precision remainder from ratio math at all — it documents a **wrong-annotation-vs-real-measurement** correction (an "X-Large = 82%" library annotation was actually mislabeled — the real Cart frame is a **fixed** 1186px, not a percentage, and separately a *different* wrong 82% figure had been mistakenly used for `Tablet`, which is genuinely 80%). That's a categorical labelling/measurement error, corrected by re-measuring real Figma frames — a different kind of problem from "67 × 432/288 = 100.5, half a pixel over a stated round number," which is a benign, unavoidable arithmetic consequence of applying one exact ratio (288/432, which is exact for the 132×198 desktop pair) to a second dimension pair that wasn't itself perfectly divisible. **CONFIRMED: this is not the same class of gap as claimed** — the citation is inaccurate, even though the underlying 100.5px value itself is not a bug (it's the mathematically correct result of the stated ratio, and half a pixel is visually immaterial). This is a documentation-precision issue in the docblock's justification, not a functional defect.
